column3: NKJV has “let us make,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “I will make.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV supplies “came” and renders “listen to Him” as “Hear Him!”
NKJV includes “first,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Elijah is coming and will restore all things.”
Close to the Greek; “unbelieving” is rendered “faithless.”
NKJV has “unbelief,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads ὀλιγοπιστίαν (“little faith”).
This verse is absent from the critical text; NKJV includes it following the Textus Receptus (“this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting”).
NKJV has “staying,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “gathering together.”
NKJV renders “the didrachmas” (a two-drachma coin) as “the temple tax.”
NKJV has “Peter said to Him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “when he said.”
NKJV renders the coin στατῆρα (“stater”) as “a piece of money.”
